categories.main_business_segments: Leon Technology primarily operates in four main segments: digital city system services, data center and cloud computing services, communication network technology services, and telecom operator value-added services. The digital city segment focuses on video surveillance systems and integrated solutions for government and enterprise clients. The data center segment involves operating multiple Tier3+ data centers and providing cloud and AI computing services. Communication network services include planning, construction, and maintenance for telecom operators and other industries. The value-added services segment offers digital media content and marketing services through telecom platforms.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced technologies such as AI, cloud computing, big data, edge computing, and video analytics in its digital city solutions. It operates Tier3+ data centers with high power efficiency (PUE ~1.243) and provides integrated 'compute+storage+network' services via its proprietary 'Leon Cloud Computing' platform. It develops proprietary AI algorithms and customized solutions including AI model production lines and intelligent monitoring systems. The communication network services utilize expertise in network design, construction, and maintenance, supported by a project-driven management system and standardized operational procedures.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Leon Technology serves a broad customer base including government agencies, telecom operators (China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom), financial institutions, agriculture, energy, water conservancy, transportation, public security, education, and internet companies. Its digital city systems primarily target government and enterprise clients. Data center and cloud services cater to internet companies, gaming, e-commerce, and cloud service providers. The telecom network services focus on telecom operators and large enterprises. The value-added services target end consumers via telecom platforms.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company is headquartered in Urumqi, Xinjiang, China, with operations covering Northwest China, Southwest China, South China, and East China. It has expanded beyond Xinjiang to multiple provinces and overseas markets including the Middle East, Central Asia, and Southeast Asia. Key data center projects are located in Chengdu (Sichuan), Guangzhou (Nansha), and other national computing hub nodes. The company also operates subsidiaries and projects in Saudi Arabia and other international locations.
categories.supply_chain_position: Leon Technology operates primarily in the midstream and downstream segments of the information technology and telecommunications supply chain. It provides integrated system solutions, network construction and maintenance services, and data center/cloud computing services. It acts as a service provider and solutions integrator rather than a raw material supplier or equipment manufacturer. Its telecom value-added services position it as a content provider and platform operator downstream in the telecom ecosystem.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company emphasizes innovation in AI, cloud computing, and digital city technologies, with ongoing R&D projects in blockchain applications, immersive digital tourism, high-density video compression, network security, and AI-powered operational platforms. It aims to enhance its AI computing capabilities, expand cloud services, and develop industry-specific AI applications. Strategic priorities include accelerating the 'East Data West Computing' initiative, expanding overseas markets, and transitioning traditional ICT services towards AICT (AI + ICT) integration. R&D investment accounted for approximately 3.47% of revenue in 2024.
categories.revenue_model: Leon Technology generates revenue primarily through direct sales of integrated digital city systems, engineering construction contracts, and ongoing system operation and maintenance services. Data center and cloud computing services generate revenue via bandwidth, cabinet, and IP address leasing, as well as value-added cloud services billed on fixed or usage-based contracts. Telecom value-added services earn revenue through content distribution, digital marketing, and mobile payment billing via telecom operator platforms. The company uses a direct sales model with pricing based on product type, region, volume, and market competition.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company holds a leading position in Xinjiang's digital city and telecom network services market and is expanding nationally and internationally. It competes with other integrated IT service providers, data center operators, and telecom value-added service companies. Leon Technology differentiates itself through its comprehensive end-to-end integration capabilities, proprietary AI and cloud computing platforms, and strong regional market penetration. Its strategic alliances with AI algorithm providers, research institutions, and telecom operators enhance its competitive edge.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Leon Technology reported operating revenue of approximately RMB 788 million, a 9.02% increase over 2023, and a net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 25.87 million, a 247.18% increase. Total assets were about RMB 2.15 billion, with net assets of RMB 1.46 billion. The company has shown steady revenue growth and improved profitability, supported by successful debt restructuring and enhanced receivables collection. R&D expenses increased by 16.32%, reflecting ongoing investment in innovation. The company operates with a workforce of over 900 employees, including 129 R&D personnel.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Leon Technology emphasizes autonomous innovation and self-controlled core technologies in digital city systems, AI computing platforms, and cloud services. Its integrated 'compute+storage+network' solution offers flexible, scalable, and cost-effective AI computing resources tailored for diverse applications such as AIGC, deep learning, cloud rendering, and industrial simulation. The company’s strong regional presence, comprehensive project execution capabilities, and strategic partnerships enable it to deliver customized, high-quality solutions that enhance urban governance, telecom network reliability, and digital transformation for clients. Its proprietary AI products and cloud platforms provide competitive differentiation in the evolving digital economy.
